evidence_text: User accounts are actively managed with defined roles. Inactive/unauthorized accounts are disabled. Account status is monitored in real time.
Role-based access control is enforced on every API endpoint via FastAPI dependency injection. Users can only access resources within their authorization level.
Privileged accounts (system_admin, security_officer) are minimized. Users are assigned the lowest role necessary for their function.
The system enforces a limit on consecutive failed login attempts and automatically locks accounts. Nginx applies network-layer rate limiting. Application-layer rate limiting is enforced via slowapi.
All remote sessions are authenticated via JWT and authorized through RBAC. Session access is controlled, monitored, and tied to authenticated user identities.
Security-relevant events are identified, classified by severity and category, and logged with sufficient detail to support investigations and forensic analysis.
Audit records include all required fields: event type, timestamp, user identity, source IP, client user-agent, affected resource, and structured metadata payload.
Audit records are append-only. No UPDATE or DELETE operations are permitted on the AuditLog table through the application layer. PostgreSQL access is restricted to the application service account.

Audit records are retained in PostgreSQL with no automated deletion policy. Retention period is determined by available storage and organizational policy. A formal retention schedule and automated purge mechanism have not been implemented.
Audit records are generated automatically for all security-relevant events throughout the system, including authentication, access control, and data operations, via the audit middleware.

System is deployed with security-hardened settings: Nginx security headers, HSTS, CSP, startup environment validation, and no permissive defaults. All configuration is sourced from environment variables.
RBAC enforces minimum necessary access. Routes require the lowest permissible role. Only required ports are exposed. Unused services are not deployed.
System recovery capability is supported by persistent PostgreSQL and Redis volumes, stateless application containers, and monitored database connections.
All users are uniquely identified by username and authenticated via password + optional MFA. All API endpoints require a valid JWT. Anonymous access is blocked except for the health check endpoint.

Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost factor 12). MFA uses RFC 6238 TOTP (pyotp). MFA adoption is not yet enforced organization-wide — 0% of users have MFA enabled, which does not meet the organizational security posture requirement.
JWT access tokens expire after 15 minutes, requiring silent refresh. Refresh tokens expire after 7 days. Token rotation prevents replay attacks.
Security incidents (account lockouts, brute-force patterns, privilege escalations) are automatically detected, classified, and logged as SecurityEvents for SOC investigation.
Security anomalies (MFA disables, role escalations, account lockouts) are automatically detected and logged as high-severity events for SOC review.
User deletions and account removals are logged and tracked. Account access is revoked immediately upon deactivation. All actions are captured in the audit log.
Rate limiting is enforced at two independent layers: Nginx network layer and the application layer via slowapi. Authentication endpoints have stricter limits than general API endpoints.
Nginx acts as the single external boundary. All traffic enters through Nginx, which enforces rate limiting and HTTP proxying to internal services. Direct backend access is not exposed.
All external traffic is TLS-encrypted via Nginx. Security headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy) are enforced at both Nginx and application layers.
JWT signing keys are cryptographically strong, securely stored in environment variables, and meet minimum length requirements. Key strength is validated at startup via pydantic-settings.

JWT tokens include issuer and audience claims that are validated on every request. Token rotation prevents replay attacks. Redis provides persistent real-time session state for refresh token revocation.

Passwords are one-way hashed with bcrypt (cost factor 12). MFA TOTP secrets are stored in the database. No plaintext credentials are stored. PostgreSQL data files are stored on a dedicated Docker volume.
Content Security Policy prevents XSS-based code injection. Input validation via Pydantic v2 sanitizes all user input. Nginx inspects request sizes and enforces content type restrictions.
